title: 5 TTS backends (f5, fish, coqui, bark, qwen) have no break-marker support -- would read pause markers as literal text
description:
Kokoro, Higgs, and Chatterbox all correctly split on AURITUS_BREAK_MARKER
and insert a real silence gap (see kokoro.py/higgs.py/chatterbox.py, and the
new shared auritus.tts.breaks / tts.breaks module both cli/ and
worker-image/ backends now import it from). f5.py, fish.py, coqui.py,
bark.py, and qwen.py have none of that -- they pass the raw text straight
to their respective models, break markers included. Since the embed
generator now inserts this marker automatically after every heading,
paragraph, list item, and blockquote (as of the pause-insertion work this
week), any of these five backends fed real article content would
synthesize the literal string '[[auritus:break]]' as spoken text at every
paragraph boundary.

Lower priority because none of the five is the default or currently
selected by any real site's embed config (kokoro is Pilobol.us's only
backend in practice) -- but the gap is real and will bite the next
integration that picks one of them without knowing to check. Each backend
needs the same three-line fix kokoro/higgs/chatterbox already have:
import AURITUS_BREAK_MARKER/split_on_breaks from the shared breaks module,
iterate blocks, join with a tuned BREAK_SILENCE_SECONDS silence gap.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Resolved for all active models: F5, Fish, and Qwen have full break and pause marker support with silence insertion as of PR #57 and PR #58. Bark and Coqui are legacy stubs.
